Students with experience in text, audio, or video journalism are invited to be part of CU-CitizenAccess.org, an award-winning online newsroom that publishes watchdog and in-depth community reporting (with an emphasis on data journalism) for central Illinois. Students will have an opportunity to produce stories that will appear on the web site and be shared with other media organizations in the state and sometimes nationally. Students will choose to pursue 2-4 credit hours based on the rubric that a minimum of forty-five hours of production activity must be completed over the course of the semester for each credit hour. Instructor's approval needed. Email Professor Houston at houstonb@illinois.edu if interested in taking this course.

IPM Reporters: Students with training or experience in audio journalism are invited to apply to be a part of the working Illinois Public Media newsroom on the U of I campus. Students will practice peer mentoring to produce work ranging from spot news to full feature stories for WILL-AM, WILL-FM and www.ipmnewsroom.org, with the chance to produce stories for a national audience. Pre-requisite: JOUR 215 or instructor approval. If interested in this course, please contact the instructor directly. Meets with JOUR 400 PM2 (71966).

IPM Senior Reporters: Students with training or experience in audio journalism are invited to be part of the working Illinois Public Media newsroom on the U of I campus. Students will practice peer mentoring to produce work ranging from spot news to full feature stories for WILL-AM, WILL-FM and www.ipmnewsroom.org, with the chance to produce stories for a national audience. Pre-requisite: JOUR 215 or instructor approval. If interested in this course, please contact the instructor directly. Meets with JOUR 400 PM1 (75689).

Data analysis and visualization have become integral parts of journalism. This class will introduce you to the basics of data journalism, including finding and downloading data and using spreadsheets and database manager software for news stories. Students will work with local and national data and learn how to combine their data analysis with interviews and field work to produce meaningful stories. Non-degree seeking students may enroll on a space-available basis with consent of the department. To request enrollment, please email journ@illinois.edu.

Today’s media consumers are increasingly reliant on visual stories. This class guides students in how to turn reporting on science research into an effective video story. Students will have a better understanding of how to structure a visual story for greater impact. Students will learn how to use video to not only expand their storytelling, but also expand their audience. Non-Degree seeking students may enroll on a space-available basis with consent of the department. To request enrollment, please email journ@illinois.edu. Upon approval, students will then need to complete an application through the Center for Innovation in Teaching & Learning to obtain permission to register: https://apps.citl.illinois.edu/non-degree-registration/NonDegreeStudents/Home

sections.sectionText: The Future of News: Trust, Democracy and AI. How should journalism evolve to serve democratic public life in an age of declining trust and rapid technological change? That's the question we will be tackling via three new books about journalism: Journalism in the Age of AI: From Acceleration to Reimagination; The Next Journalism: How the Press Must Change to Serve Democracy; and Does Trust Matter? Why Journalists Need to Rethink the Relationship with Their Audience. Through a variety of short writing assignments, discussion, group activities and final project, our goal will be to learn what the authors have to say, but, just as importantly, what we can or should do about it.
